Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Anjani Kumar Sharan
 Oral Order
3 19-06-2023
Heard learned counsel for the for the petitioner, learned counsel for the informant/complainant and learned APP for the State.
The petitioner apprehends his arrest in a case registered for the offences punishable under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code and Section  of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
Petitioner, who is husband of informant/complainant, is said to have ousted her from the matrimonial home in association of his family members over the dowry demand.
It is submitted by learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is an innocent person and has committed no Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.3400 of 2023(3) dt.19-06-2023 offence.

Petitioner has neither made any dowry demand nor drove her out of her matrimonial home nor Bikku Kumar @ Biku Kumar @ Bikki Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137823208/
1 tormented her over the demand of dowry.

sentences.text:
In that view of the matter, let the above named petitioner, be released on bail, in the event of his arrest or surrender before the learned Court below within a period of six weeks from today, on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Court below where the case is pending/successor Court in connection with Complaint Case No.1027C of 2022, subject to the condition as laid down under Section 438 (2) of the Cr.P.C., Petitioner is ready to pay Rs.4000.00 (Rupees Four Thousand)
per month to the informant/complainant in the second week of every month.

If the petitioner fails to pay the aforesaid amount on two consecutive months, informant/complainant shall be at liberty to move before the learned Court below for cancelling the bail bond of the petitioner.

Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.3400 of 2023(3) dt.19-06-2023 It goes without saying that the aforesaid payment shall be subject to any order being passed in matrimonial maintenance case or any other collateral proceedings.
Learned counsel for the informant/complainant is directed to furnish the bank account details of the informant/complainant in the learned Court below.

If she fails to furnish the same, the aforesaid amount will be deposited in the learned Court below which will be released in favour of the informant/complainant after she furnishes her bank account details.

If so advised, either of the parties will be at liberty to make an application before the learned Court below for referring the matter to the District Mediation Center for the purpose of reconciliation or one time settlement.
With the aforesaid observation and direction, this application stands disposed of.

(Anjani Kumar Sharan, J) shikha/-
